a46.t:
Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria, and Ukraine could soon run out of these life-saving medicines, WHO said Monday.
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned that the Trump administration’s decision to pause U.S. foreign aid has "substantially disrupted" the supply of HIV treatments in eight countries, putting millions at risk.
Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria, and Ukraine could soon run out of these life-saving medicines, WHO said Monday.
"The disruptions to HIV programs could undo 20 years of progress," WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus cautioned at a press conference.
He warned that this setback could lead to over 10 million new HIV cases and three million HIV-related deaths.
The U.S. aid freeze, implemented by President Donald Trump shortly after taking office in January, has also impacted efforts to fight polio, malaria, and tuberculosis.
Additionally, the WHO-coordinated Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network—operating over 700 sites worldwide—faces an imminent shutdown.
This comes as measles cases resurge in the United States.
"The United States has a responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws funding, it does so in an orderly and humane way that allows affected countries to find alternative resources," Ghebreyesus stressed.
Beyond HIV treatment shortages, WHO has warned of severe consequences in Afghanistan. As of March 4, 167 health facilities have shut down due to funding shortages, and over 220 more could close by June without urgent intervention. WHO estimates that 80% of its supported essential healthcare services in Afghanistan are at risk.
Meanwhile, the U.S. decision to withdraw from WHO has forced the agency— which typically receives about a fifth of its annual funding from the U.S.— to freeze hiring and impose budget cuts
It would be recalled that Trump administration stopped support for international health programs in its “cut-down” in the cost of administration in the country.
The development has however been met with mixed reactions and warnings on repercussions across board.

a249.t:
Tahoua,16 juin (ANP) – Les fidèles musulmans de la Communauté Urbaine de Tahoua ont célébré, ce dimanche 16 juin 2024, la fête de Tabaski dans la communion des cœurs. Très tôt le matin, des milliers de fidèles musulmans ont pris d’assaut la mosquée des grandes prières vêtus de leurs beaux habits pour accomplir la prière d’Aîd Al Adha.
Après l’accomplissement des deux rakaats, l’Imâm prononça son sermon, dans lequel il a abordé l’importance du sacrifice lors de cette fête, mais a aussi traité de l’unité et de l’aide entre les musulmans. Parlant du sacrifice, il a notamment énuméré les différents animaux pour le sacrifice que sont le mouton et/ou la brebis, le bouc et/ou la chèvre, le taureau et/ou la vache, le chameau et/ou la chamelle, qui devront tous être en bonne santé.
Et l’on doit, selon lui, partager la viande en trois parties entre la famille, les amis et les nécessiteux.
L’Imâm a ensuite prié pour la paix et la prospérité du Niger, avant de procéder à l’immolation de son mouton donnant ainsi le coup d’envoi au sacrifice d’Abraham.
Les autorités régionales ayant pris part à cette prière ont présente leurs meilleurs vœux de bonne fête à la population. Le Gouverneur de la région de Tahoua Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé s’est réjoui de la célébration de cette fête et a demandé aux oulémas de continuer la prière pour la paix et la stabilité dans le pays.
Le Ministre de l’Agriculture et de l’Elevage Mahamane Elhadj Ousmane, en mission dans la Région, a également présenté ses meilleurs vœux de bonne fête à l’ensemble des populations du pays, et a émis le souhait que cette fête puisse apporter le bonheur, la paix et la communion entre les différentes communautés pays. Il a aussi prié pour un hivernage fécond dans le pays.
»Je suis en visite dans la région de Tahoua depuis quelques jours, nous avons vu la résilience de la population. Nous leur demandons de se pardonner, de s’unir pour réussir ce combat noble de la refondation du Niger », a indiqué le Ministre Ousmane.
Il faut retenir aussi que l’Administrateur Délégué de la ville de Tahoua Sahabi Moussa et le Chef du Canton de Tahoua ont tour à tour pris la parole pour présenter leurs meilleurs vœux de bonne fête et demander pardon à la population de la ville de Tahoua.
TSA/KPM/ANP- Juin 2024
a249.en:
Tahoua: Eid al-Adha celebrated in communion of hearts

Tahoua, 16 June (ANP) – The Muslim faithful of the Urban Community of Tahoua celebrated, on Sunday 16 June 2024, the Tabaski festival in communion of hearts. Very early in the morning, thousands of Muslim faithful took over the great prayer mosque, dressed in their finest clothes, to perform the Eid al-Adha prayer.

After completing the two rakaats, the Imam delivered his sermon, in which he addressed the importance of sacrifice during this festival, but also dealt with unity and mutual assistance among Muslims. Speaking of sacrifice, he notably listed the various animals for the sacrifice, namely the ram and/or the ewe, the billy goat and/or the she-goat, the bull and/or the cow, the male camel and/or the she-camel, all of which must be in good health.

And one must, according to him, share the meat in three parts among family, friends and the needy.

The Imam then prayed for peace and prosperity in Niger, before proceeding to the slaughter of his ram, thus giving the starting signal for the sacrifice of Abraham.

The regional authorities who took part in this prayer presented their best wishes for a happy feast to the population. The Governor of the Tahoua region, Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, expressed his delight at the celebration of this festival and asked the ulema to continue praying for peace and stability in the country.

The Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Mahamane Elhadj Ousmane, on mission in the Region, also presented his best wishes for a happy feast to all the populations of the country, and expressed the wish that this festival might bring happiness, peace and communion among the country's different communities. He also prayed for a fruitful rainy season in the country.

"I have been visiting the Tahoua region for a few days; we have seen the resilience of the population. We ask them to forgive one another, to unite in order to succeed in this noble struggle for the refoundation of Niger," said Minister Ousmane.

It should also be noted that the Delegated Administrator of the city of Tahoua, Sahabi Moussa, and the Chief of the Canton of Tahoua each in turn took the floor to present their best wishes for a happy feast and to ask forgiveness from the population of the city of Tahoua.

TSA/KPM/ANP - June 2024

a250.t:
Ojuiz Amir Ali emitiu a ordem na quinta-feira, no tribunal distrital dos EUA em Washington, numa acção interposta por duas organizações de saúde que recebem financiamento dos EUA para programas no estrangeiro.
Na ordem, Ali observou que o Governo argumentou que precisava de congelar o financiamento de milhares de programas de ajuda da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID, na sigla em inglês) no estrangeiro para conduzir uma revisão completa de cada programa e se deveriam ser eliminados.
No entanto, os funcionários do Governo "não ofereceram qualquer explicação" sobre o motivo pelo qual a suspensão de toda a ajuda externa, "que desencadeou uma onda de choque e derrubou" contratos com milhares de grupos sem fins lucrativos, empresas e outros "foi um precursor racional para a revisão de programas", disse o juiz.
A decisão foi a primeira a reverter temporariamente a ordem do novo Presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, que suspendeu toda a ajuda internacional durante 90 dias, com excepção dos programas humanitários alimentares e da ajuda militar a Israel e ao Egipto.
Trump obrigou a USAID e os contratados do Departamento de Estado em todo o mundo a deixar de prestar ajuda humanitária e outras formas de assistência e a despedir funcionários, paralisando grande parte das redes de distribuição de ajuda do mundo.
A ordem que permite o regresso dos fundos aplica-se aos contratos existentes antes de Trump emitir a ordem executiva de 20 de Janeiro, declarando o congelamento da assistência estrangeira.
Trump classificou grande parte da ajuda dos EUA de desalinhada com a sua agenda.
O secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio, é o novo director interino da USAID, que acusou de estar "completamente desprovida de capacidade de resposta", criticando o que descreveu como insubordinação naquele organismo.
Também na quinta-feira, num caso separado, um juiz manteve, durante pelo menos mais uma semana, a suspensão da ordem emitida por Trump para retirar a esmagadora maioria dos funcionários da USAID destacados em todo o mundo.
O juiz distrital, Carl Nichols, ordenou a extensão após uma audiência de quase três horas na quinta-feira, grande parte dela focada na forma como os funcionários foram afectados por ordens abruptas da administração Trump e do aliado Elon Musk, que lidera o Departamento de Eficiência Governamental.
Funcionários da USAID que estavam destacados na República Democrática do Congo disseram que a agência praticamente os abandonou quando os saques e a violência política explodiram no leste do país africano em Janeiro, obrigando-os a fugir com as famílias.
a250.en:
Judge Amir Ali issued the order on Thursday in the US district court in Washington, in a case brought by two health organisations that receive US funding for programmes abroad.

In the order, Ali noted that the Government had argued that it needed to freeze the funding of thousands of aid programmes of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) abroad in order to conduct a full review of each programme and of whether they should be eliminated.

However, Government officials "offered no explanation" as to why the suspension of all foreign aid, "which set off a shockwave and brought down" contracts with thousands of non-profit groups, companies and others, "was a rational precursor to the review of programmes", the judge said.

The decision was the first to temporarily reverse the order of the new US President, Donald Trump, who suspended all international aid for 90 days, with the exception of humanitarian food programmes and military aid to Israel and Egypt.

Trump forced USAID and State Department contractors around the world to stop providing humanitarian aid and other forms of assistance and to dismiss staff, paralysing much of the world's aid distribution networks.

The order allowing the return of the funds applies to contracts existing before Trump issued the executive order of 20 January declaring the freeze on foreign assistance.

Trump classified much of US aid as misaligned with his agenda.

The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, is the new acting director of USAID, which he accused of being "completely devoid of responsiveness", criticising what he described as insubordination within that body.

Also on Thursday, in a separate case, a judge maintained, for at least another week, the suspension of the order issued by Trump to withdraw the overwhelming majority of USAID staff posted around the world.

The district judge, Carl Nichols, ordered the extension after a hearing of almost three hours on Thursday, much of it focused on how staff were affected by abrupt orders from the Trump administration and its ally Elon Musk, who leads the Department of Government Efficiency.

USAID staff who were posted in the Democratic Republic of Congo said that the agency practically abandoned them when looting and political violence erupted in the east of that African country in January, forcing them to flee with their families.

a282.t:
The Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency (ATA) and Save the Children in Ethiopia signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to use the 8028 Farmers’ Hotline in order to deliver nutrition-sensitive agricultural messages.
The duo has agreed to utilize the Interactive Voice Response/Short Message Service (IVR/SMS) to farmers for advice on nutrition-sensitive agriculture.
“Even if nutrition is a clear human health issue it also has a direct relationship with the farmers and the agriculture directly,” said Kalidbomba. “The success of the hotline in this short period of time is derived by the high demand of the farmers to access helpful information.”
“It is a smart and timely information dissemination tool which is enabled by this partnership with ATA,” said Ekin Ogutogullari, Country Director of Save the Children in Ethiopia. “It helps us avoid duplication of efforts and wisely use available resources and it will contribute to the dietary consumption behavior improvement of farmers.”
The USAID funded Growth through Nutrition (GTN) program is implemented by Save the Children in Ethiopia and works to strengthen Ethiopia’s institutions, systems, and human capacity to improve nutrition and significantly reduce stunting.

a586.t: O Millennium Challenge Corporation, MCC, aprovou, ontem, um financiamento de 500 milhões de dólares norte-americanos para a implementação do Compacto-II em Moçambique. Segundo um comunicado enviado à nossa redacção, a assinatura do Acordo de Financiamento entre os Governos de Moçambique e dos Estados Unidos, através do MCC, está prevista para Setembro deste ano, em Washington DC. O compacto-II, aprovado em Washington, nos Estados Unidos da América, terá como enfoque a província da Zambézia, cobrindo três áreas: Promoção de Investimento na Agricultura Comercial; Conectividade e Transporte Rural, Mudanças Climáticas e Desenvolvimento Costeiro.
a586.en:
Millennium Challenge Corporation approves 500 million USD for Mozambique's Compact II programme

The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) yesterday approved financing of 500 million US dollars for the implementation of Compact II in Mozambique. According to a statement sent to our newsroom, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is scheduled for September this year in Washington DC. Compact II, approved in Washington, in the United States of America, will focus on Zambézia province, covering three areas: Promotion of Investment in Commercial Agriculture; Rural Connectivity and Transport; and Climate Change and Coastal Development.

a616.t:
የኢትዮጵያ አትሌቲክስ ፌዴሬሽን የፕሬዚዳንትና የሥራ አስፈጻሚ ኮሚቴ ምርጫ በሚቀጥለው ቅዳሜና እሑድ በአዲስ አበባ ስካይ ላይት ሆቴል ይደረጋል፡፡ ለፕሬዚዳንታዊው ምርጫ ከሚወዳደሩት መካከል ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ ገረመው አንዱ ናቸው፡፡ ከድሬዳዋ ከተማ አስተዳደር የተወከሉት ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፣ የኢትዮጵያ ኤሌክትሪክ አገልግሎት ምክትል ዋና ሥራ አስፈጻሚ እንዲሁም የኢትዮ ኤሌክትሪክ ስፖርት ክለብ ምክትል ቦርድ ሰብሳቢ ሆነው በማገልገል ላይ ይገኛሉ፡፡
ለአትሌቲክሱ ቅርበት ካላቸው ቤተሰቦች መገኘታቸውን የሚገልጹት ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፣ በተለይም በአሁኑ ወቅት፣ ካለበት የአደረጃጀት ክፍተት፣ ከአትሌት ምርጫና ምልመላ፣ ከሠልጣኞች ምርጫና ደረጃ እንዲሁም ከማናጀሮች የኃላፊነት ገደብ ማለትም የዕውቅና (ሠርተፍኬሸን) አሰጣጥ ሒደትና ተያያዥ ተግዳሮቶች እንዳሉበት የሚነገርለትን ይህን ፌዴሬሽን ለመምራት ይዘውት በመጡት ዕቅድ ዙሪያ ደረጀ ጠገናው አነጋግሯቸዋል፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- የኢትዮጵያ አትሌቲክስ ፌዴሬሽን ዓለም አቀፍ እውቅና እና ዝና ማትረፍ የቻሉ ታላላቅ አትሌቶችን ማፍራት የቻለ፣ ነገር ግን ደግሞ የአደረጃጀትና የአሠራር ክፍተት እንዳለበት ይነገራል፡፡ እርስዎ ይህን ተቋም ለመምራት ምን ዓይነት ዕቅድ ይዘው ለምርጫ ቀረቡ?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- የኢትዮጵያ አትሌቲክስ በትውልድ ቅብብሎሽ የመጣበት ሒደትና ስፖርቱን ለሚወድ እንደ አንድ ኢትዮጵያዊ፣ ተቋሙ አልፎ አልፎ የውዝግብና የንትርክ መንስዔ ሲሆን በጣም ይገርመኛል፣ ያመኛልም፡፡ ምክንያቱም አትሌቲክስ ተወደደም ተጠላም ዓይነተኛ የዲፕሎማሲያችን መገለጫ ብቻ ሳይሆን የአሸናፊነታችን ምልክት ነው፡፡ ትልቅ የኢንቨስትመንት አማራጭም ሆኗል፡፡ ስፖርቱ የሚገኝበት ደረጃና ቁመና በዚህ ልክ ከሆነ ታዲያ የሚመጥነውን ቁመና ማሲያዝና ማደራጀት ለምን ተሳነን የሚለው በውስጤ የሚመላለስ አሁንም ያለ ቁጭት ነው፡፡ ለውድድር ዕጩ ሆኜ ቀርቤያለሁ፣ ዕድሉን ካገኘሁ ተቋሙን ለማዘመን ዝግጁ ነኝ፡፡ በሙያዬ ኤሌክትሪካል መሃንዲስ ነኝ፣ የምመራው ተቋም ደግሞ የኢትዮጵያ ኤሌክትሪክ አገልግሎት ሲሆን፣ ኃላፊነቴም ምክትል ዋና ሥራ አስፈጻሚ ነው፡፡ በምመራው ተቋም ሥር የሚተዳደሩ የአትሌቲክስ፣ የእግር ኳስና የቴኒስ ክለቦች ምክትል ቦርድ ሰብሳቢ እንደመሆኔ፣ ሦስቱንም ክለቦች ማሻሻያ (ሪፎርም) በማድረግ ከአገሪቱ የስፖርት ክለቦች የተሻለ አደረጃጀት እንዲኖራቸው ከባልደረቦቼ ጋር ሠርቻለሁ፣ እየሠራሁም እገኛለሁ፡፡ ለአትሌቲክስ ልዩ ፍቅርና ክብር አለኝ፣ ከቤተሰቦቼ አራቱ አትሌቶች ናቸው፡፡ እኔን በሚመለከት ለትምህርት በነበረኝ ፍላጎት ብዙም ባልገፋበትም ከትምህርት ቤት ጀምሮ ሯጭ ነበርኩ፡፡ ላለፉት ሁለት አሠርታት ያህል ከማዘውተሪያዎች ጀምሮ አትሌቲክስን በማገዝና በመደገፍ የተለያዩ ሥራዎችን እያከናወንኩ እገኛለሁ፡፡ ይህ ተሞክሮዬ ነው ትልቁን ተቋም እንድመራ መነሻ የሆነኝ፡፡ በእርግጠኝነት ዕድሉን ካገኘሁ ተቋሙን ከአደረጃጀት ጀምሮ ጊዜውን የሚመጥን ትክክለኛ ቁመና እንዲኖረው እሠራለሁ፣ አሳካዋለሁም፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- ፌዴሬሽኑ በአግባቡ እየተመራ እንዳልሆነ ይነገራል፡፡ እርስዎ ይህንን እንዴት ይገልጹታል?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- ለስፖርቱ ቅርብ ነኝ ስል እንደ ብሔራዊ ተቋም በውስጡ ያሉትንና የሚስተዋሉ ክፍተቶችና ችግሮች ምን እንደሚመስሉ አውቃለሁ፣ እሰማለሁም፡፡ ስፖርት እንዴት እንደሚመራ ስፖርት አመራር ምን እንደሆነ ላለፉት ስድስት ዓመታት የቆየሁበት ዘርፍ በመሆኑ አውቀዋለሁ፡፡ ከዚህም በላይ በተለያዩ የሥራ አጋጣሚዎች ከፌዴሬሽኑ አመራሮችና ባለሙያዎች ጋር በምናደርጋቸው ውይይቶች፣ እዚያ አካባቢ የሚፈጠሩ አለመግባባቶች ምን እንደሆኑ ከነምክንያቶቻቸው ጭምር በቅርበት የማውቃቸው ናቸው፡፡ ባለፉት ሁለትና ሦስት ኦሊምፒኮች እንዲሁም የዓለም አትሌቲክስ ሻምፒዮናዎች ላይ በራሴ ወጪ የመታደም ዕድሉ ስለነበረኝ፣ የነበሩ ክፍተቶች እንዴትና ለምን ሊፈጠሩ እንደቻሉ መፍትሔያቸውንም ጭምር አስተዳደር ላይ እንደሚገኝ ሰው አውቄያለሁ፣ እረዳለሁ፡፡ ቤቱ ሮጠህ ስላሳለፍክ አልያም የሩጫ ሳይንስ ስላወቅህ ብቻ የምትመራው ተቋም ነው የሚል እምነት የለኝም፡፡ ስለሆነም ተቋሙ የጎደለው ብትለኝ፣ የመምራት ብቃት (ሊደርሺፕ ኳሊቲ) ነው፡፡ ይህን የምለው ዝም ብዬ ሳይሆን ከሪዮ እስከ ፓሪስ ኦሊምፒክ ሦስትና ከዚህም በላይ የወርቅ ሜዳሊያ ማምጣት የሚችሉ አቅሙ ያላቸው አትሌቶች ነበሩ፡፡ ነገር ግን ሁሉም እንደሚያውቀው በነበረው ችግር ምክንያት ማቀናጀት ስላልተቻለ ብቻ ውጤት ጠፋ፡፡ በዚህ ረገድ ባለኝ ተሞክሮና ልምድ ተቋሙን ለማስተካከልና ለመምራት ብቁም ዝግጁም ነኝ፡፡ ከባለድርሻ አካላት ጋር ግልጽና አሳታፊ ውይይቶችን በማድረግ ኦሊምፒክና የዓለም አትሌቲክስ ሻምፒዮናዎች ሲመጡ የሚያለቅሱ አትሌቶች ብሶትና እሮሮ፣ ሥርዓትና መመርያዎችን በማዘጋጀት የመፍትሔው አካል ለመሆን ነው ወደ ተቋሙ የምመጣው፡፡ በግሌ ምርጫ ከመምጣቱ ስድስት ወርና ከዚያም በፊት ሁሉም የሚስማማበትና የሚያምንበት መሥፈርት (ክራይቴሪያ) በጋራ ማውጣት ከተቻለ አሁን ላይ የምንሰማቸው ክርክሮችና ጭቅጭቆች ሊኖሩ አይችሉም፡፡ መሥፈርቱ ሲወጣ ለዚህ ቅርብ የሆኑ ባለሙያዎች፣ የክለብ አመራሮችና ሌሎችም የሚመለከታቸው ባለድርሻ አካላት እንዲሳተፉበት፣ እንዲመክሩበት፣ እንዲወስኑበት ዕድሉን የሚያገኙ ከሆነ ሁሉም ነገር መፍትሔ አገኘ ማለት ነው፡፡ አንድ መሪ አሠልጣኝ አልያም የቴክኒክ ባለሙያ እንዲሆን አይጠበቅም፣ ማድረግ የሚጠበቅበት ዕድሉን ለሚመለከታቸው ክፍሎች (ዲፓርትመንት) ማድረስ፣ ማውረድ ነው፡፡ ይህን ለማድረግ ትልቅ ተቋም የምመራ ሰው በመሆኔ ብቻ ሳይሆን፣ ፍቅሩም ስላለኝ ይከብደኛል የሚል እምነት የለኝም፡፡ ቀላልም ነው፡፡ አትሌቶችን ለማብቃት በክልልና በወረዳ፣ በክለብ ደረጃም ወርዶ ለመሥራት ከትምህርት ዝግጅቴ ጀምሮ ሰብዕናዬ የሚፈቅድልኝ ስለሆነ ፌዴሬሽኑን በቅጡና በአግባቡ ለመምራት ዝግጁ ነኝ፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- አትሌቲክሱ በአሁኑ ወቅት የብዙ ሰዎችን ፍላጎትና ስሜት የሚገዛ፣ ከዚህም ሲያልፍ ፖለቲካዊና ሃይማኖታዊ አዝማሚያም የሚያንፀባረቅበት ዘርፍ ሆኗል፡፡ ይህን ስፖርቱ ከሚመራበት ሕግጋት ጋር አጣጥሞ ለመሃድ ምን ያህል ዝግጁ ነዎት?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- የተነሱት ችግሮች ስፖርቱ ላይ በስፋት ሲንፀባረቁ ይታያል፡፡ ስፖርት ከብሔር፣ ከፆታ፣ ከባህልና ከሠፈር፣ ከቋንቋ፣ ከዘርና መሰል ነገሮች የፀዳ ስለመሆኑ ሕግጋቱ ይደነግጋል፡፡ ስፖርት ከመንደር ወጣ ያለ፣ የአንድ መንደር ዕይታን የማይመጥን፣ ይልቅስ ከዚህ በተጓዳኝ ትልቅ ትርጉም ያለው ዘርፍ ነው፡፡ ስለሆነም ይህን ሥርዓት አስይዞ መምራት ከሚመለከታቸው አካላት ጋር መነጋገር፣ መወያየትና ሥርዓት ማስቀመጥ ተገቢ መሆኑ እንደተጠበቀ ሆኖ ማለት ነው፡፡ ከውጭ ምንዛሪና ከማናጀሮች ጋር ያለው ነገር፣ ጉዳዩ ብዙ ጊዜ ሲነሳ እሰማለሁ፡፡ መፍትሔው የሥራ ድርሻን መለየትና ቀምሮ በማስቀመጥ ያንን መነሻ በማድረግ ማስቀጠልን የሚጠይቅ ነው፡፡ በዚህ ስፖርት አገር ማግኘት ስለሚገባት ጥቅም፣ እርግጠኛ ነኝ ሥርዓቱና የሥራ ድርሻዎች ከተቀመጡ ያንን የማያከብር የአትሌት ማኔጀር ይኖራል ብዬ አላስብም፡፡ ምክንያቱም እነዚሁ ማኔጀሮች በኬንያና በሌሎችም መሰል አገሮች ተመሳሳይ ሥራ በተመሳሳይ ዘርፍ ሥርዓትና መመርያን አክብረው እንደሚሠሩ ይታወቃል፡፡ በኢትዮጵያ የተለየ የሚሆንበት ምክንያት አይታየኝም፡፡ ይልቁንስ ማኔጀሮች በእኔ ዘመን ካምፖችንና አካዴሚዎችን መገንባት ይኖርባቸዋል፡፡ ያንን ተፈጻሚ የማያደርጉ ከሆነና ቀደም ሲል የገለጽኳቸውን መመርያና ደንቦች የማያከብሩ ከሆነ ከባድ ነው የሚሆንባቸው፡፡ ምክንያቱም በጎረቤት ኬንያ በተመሳሳይ የሥራ ዘርፍ የተሰማሩ ማናጀሮች ብዙ ካምፖችን እየገነቡ፣ ወጣቶችን እያሳደጉና እያበቁ ዓለም ላይ የተለያዩ ክብረ ወሰኖችን የሚያስመዘግቡ አትሌቶች ሲያፈሩ እያየን ነው፡፡ በዚያው በኬንያ ‹‹አይተን›› የሚባል ካምፕ የመመልከት ዕድሉን አግኝቻለሁ፡፡ ስለዚህ ሥርዓቱ ቢቀመጥና ተገቢው ክትትል ቢኖር፣ ከዚያ አፈንግጦ የሚወጣ ማናጀር ይኖራል ብዬ አላስብም፡፡ እርግጥ ነው ሥርዓቱን ለማስፈን ሁሉም በባለቤትነት ሊከተለው የሚገባ ጉዳይ ብቻ ሳይሆን ከዚህ ስፖርት አገር የሚገባትን የውጪ ምንዛሪ እንድታገኝ፣ የስፖርት መሠረተ ልማት እንዲስፋፋ የውዴታ ግዴታ መሆኑን አምኖ መቀበል መቻል ያስፈልግል፡፡ ለዚህም ነው ቀደም ሲል ተቋሙ የሊደርሺፕ ክፍተት አለበት የሚለውን እንዳምን ያስገደደኝ፡፡ የሚገርመው ኢትዮጵያ በአትሌቲክሱ ዓለም ላይ አንቱ የተባሉ ታላላቅ አትሌቶችን ያፈራች እንደመሆኗ ዓለም አቀፍ የስፖርት ተቋማት ውስጥ ግን አንድ እንኳ ተወካይ ሲኖራት ተመልክተን አናውቅም፡፡ ይህ ከየትም ሳይሆን ከአመራር ክፍተት የሚመጣ ችግር ነው፣ በግሌ ይሰማኛል፡፡ በተለያዩ አገሮች ባገኘሁት የመንቀሳቀስ ዕድል የወርልድ አትሌቲክስ አመራሮችን ጨምሮ ብዙዎቹን የማነጋገር አጋጣሚውን አግኝቻለሁ፡፡ ዓላማዬ እዚህ መቅረት ሳይሆን፣ በወልርድ አትሌቲክስ ደረጃ ኢትዮጵያ በዲፕሎማሲው ጭምር የሚገባትን ቦታ እንድታገኝ ማስቻል ነው፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- የአትሌቲክሱን ውድቀት፣ ከብሔራዊ ቡድን መፍረስ ጋር የሚያይዙት ሰዎች አሉ፡፡ በዚህ ጉዳይ ያለዎት አስተያየት እንዴት ይገለጻል?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- ሁሌም እንዲነሳልኝ የምፈልገው ጥያቄ ቢኖር ይህ ነው፡፡ ኢትዮጵያ በተለያዩ ዓለም አቀፍ የስፖርት መድረኮች አምራና ደምቃ እንድትታይ ከሚያስችሉ መሠረታዊ ነገሮች የብሔራዊ ቡድን ጉዳይ ቀዳሚው ነው፡፡ አገር ሲታሰብ ቀድሞ መታሰብ ያለበት የብሔራዊ ቡድን ጉዳይ ሊሆን ይገባል፡፡ የተበታተነ ቡድን አቅም የለውም፡፡ በዚህ ጉዳይ ብዙ ርቀት ሳንሄድ ወልደመስቀል ኮስትሬ (ዶ/ር) በነበሩበት ዘመን የነበረውን ብሔራዊ ቡድን መመልከት ይበቃል፡፡ የአትሌቶቻችን የአንድነት መንፈስ (ቲም ስፕሪት) ብቻውን አሸናፊ ሲያደርጋቸው የቅርብ ጊዜ ትውስታችን ነው፡፡ በኦሊምፒክም ሆነ በዓለም አትሌቲክስ ሻምፒዮና አሸንፈው ከሚያስመዘግቡት የወርቅ ሜዳሊያ በላይ በፍጹም ወንድማማችነትና እህትማማችነት ለሰንደቅ ዓላማቸው የሚሰጡት ክብር ምን ያህል አስደማሚ እንደነበር እናስታውሳለን፡፡ ያ ጊዜ ለትውልዱ የማይረሳ አሻራ ጥሎ ያለፈ ነው፡፡ በአሁኑ ወቅትስ ሜዳሊያ እንኳ ተመዝግቦ ያንን ያለፈውን ዓይነት መንፈስ አንመለከትም፡፡ ለምን፣ የተሠራ ምንም ነገር የለም፡፡ ለዚህ ምክንያት ከተባልኩ ያለምንም ማወላዳት የብሔራዊ ቡድን መፍረስ አልያም መበተን ነው፡፡ እንደ ትልቅ ክፍተትም የማየው ነው፡፡ ክፍተቱ ሰፊ በመሆኑ ዕድሉን ካገኘሁ ጉዳዩ የብዙ ባለድርሻ አካላትን የሚመለከት ስለሆነ በጋራ ተወያይተንና መክረን የምናሳካው እንደሚሆን አምናለሁ፡፡ በአትሌቲክሱ የጠፋውን የትብበርና የአንድነት መንፈስ መመለስ በዋናነት የምሠራበት ይሆናል፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- ከአሠልጣኞች ደረጃ አሰጣጥ (ሠርተፍኬሽን) ሒደት ጋር ተያይዞ የሚነሳ ጉድለት እንዳለ ይታመናል፡፡ እዚህ ላይስ ምን ዓይነት ዕቅድ አለዎት?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- ጉዳዩ በእርግጥ መምከር ይፈልጋል፣ በእኔ እምነት ግን ጉዳዩን በሦስት ከፍሎ መመልከት እንደሚያስፈልግ አምናለሁ፡፡ ምክንያቱም ባለሙያውን የሚመጥነው ሙያ (ደረጃ) ላይ ማስቀመጥ ወሳኝ ስለሆነ ነው፡፡ የአሠልጣኙ ደረጃ (ሠርተፍኬሽኑ) ከተለየ በኋላ ደግሞ የታዳጊው፣ የወጣቱ፣ አልያም የዋናው ቡድን የሚለውን በትክክል በመለየት ተግባራዊ መደረግ ስለሚኖርበት ሥራው ከዋና ዋና ዕቅዶቼ አንዱ ነው፡፡ እዚህ ላይ በግልጽ መነጋገር ይኖርብናል የሚል እምነትም ስላለኝ፣ በተቋሙ ውስጥ ለልዩነቶች መንስዔ ከሆኑ ጉዳዮች መካከል የሠርተፍኬሽን ጉዳይ ብቻ ሳይሆን፣ ከውጪ ጉዞ ጋር ተያይዞ በራሱ ማን ምን ሠርቶ ነው የሚል ነገርም ስላለ፣ አሠራሩ በግልጽ ተቀምሮ መቀመጥ ይኖርበታል፡፡ ምክንያቱም የሠራ ሰው የድካሙንና የልፋቱን ዋጋ ማግኘት ይኖርበታል የሚል እምነት ስላለኝ ማለት ነው፡፡
ሪፖርተር፡- ከማዘውተሪያ ሥፍራ ጋር ተያይዞ የፌዴሬሽኑ ትልቅ ተግዳሮት መሆኑ ይታወቃል፡፡ በዚህ ረገድስ ዕቅድዎ ምንድነው?
ኢንስፔክተር ጌቱ፡- ኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ አሁን ላይ የምናውቃቸው በተለያየ የኢንቨስትመንት ዘርፍ ተሰማርተው የምንመለከታቸው የቀድሞ አትሌቶቻችን ለታላቅ ዕውቅና የበቁት፣ ብዙ መከራና አስቸጋሪ ሁኔታዎችን አልፈው እንደሆነ የሚካድ አይደለም፡፡ በአሁኑ ወቅት ድሮ በነበረው ዓይነት አካሄድና አሠለጣጠን ውጤታማ እንሆናለን ብሎ ማሰብ የዋህነት ይመስለኛል፡፡ ዛሬ ላይ ለውጤት ከልምምድና ሩጫ ጎን ለጎን ብዙ ምርምሮች፣ የምግብና የአመጋገብ ዘይቤዎች፣ የልምምድ ቦታዎች፣ የሥልጠናና ተያያዥ ጉዳዮች የሚካተቱበት ጊዜ ነው፡፡ የተሻሉ ማዘውተሪያ ሥፍራዎች መሠራትና መገንባት የግድ የሚልበት ወቅት ላይ ነን፡፡ ይህ ካልሆነ ብዙ የምንልለት፣ የምንጓጓለት አትሌቲክሳችን ዋጋ የሚከፍልበት ጊዜ ሩቅ አይሆንም፡፡ ኅብረተሰቡ በራሱና በአካባቢው ባለቤት ሆኖ የሚስተዳድራቸው መለስተኛ ማዘውተሪያዎች እንዲገነቡ ማድረግ ያስፈልጋል፡፡ ከዚህ ባለፈ ኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ እንደ ኢትዮጵያ አየር መንገድና ኢትዮ ቴሌኮም እንዲሁም እኔ የምመራውን ተቋም ጨምሮ የማሳመን ሥራ በመሥራት ስፖርቱን እንዲደግፉ፣ ባለቤትም እንዲሆኑ ማድረግ ያስፈልጋል፡፡ እንደ ትራክና የመሳሰሉ ማዘውተሪያዎችን በተመለከተ ዓለም ላይ እንደነ አዲዳስና ናይኪ የመሳሰሉ ትጥቅ አምራች ካምፓኒዎችና ማኔጀሮች ጋር አብሮ መሥራት ያስፈልጋል፡፡ እኔ ያለሁበት ተቋም ውስጥ ጎፋ መብራት ኃይል አካባቢ ትራክ የማንጠፍ ሥራ እያስጀመርኩ ነው፡፡ ዕድሉን አግኝቼ ወደ ተቋሙ የምመጣ ከሆነ ከሚመለከታቸው ባለድርሻ አካላት ጋር በጋራ፣ በዚህ ደረጃ ያለብንን ችግር መቅረፍ የሚያስችል ሥራ ለመሥራት ዕቅድ አለኝ፡፡ በተጨማሪም ዝቅተኛ በሆኑ የአገራችን ክፍሎች ትራክ እያበዙ፣ አትሌቶች በከፍተኛ ቦታ እንዲኖሩ ማድረግን የሚያካትት ሥራ ለመሥራት ዝግጁ ነኝ፡፡ ከሁሉ ላይ ግን ነባር አትሌቶች ከተቋሙ ጋር ተቀራርበው ምክራቸውን፣ ልምዳቸውንና ተሞክሮዋቸውን እንዲያካፍሉ ማድረግ ተገቢ ስለሆነ ይህን ለማድረግ እሠራለሁ፡፡
a616.en:
The election of the president and the executive committee of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation will be held next Saturday and Sunday at the Skylight Hotel in Addis Ababa. Inspector Getu Geremew is one of those contesting the presidency. Representing the Dire Dawa City Administration, Inspector Getu currently serves as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ethiopian Electric Utility and as deputy board chairman of the Ethio Electric Sports Club.

Inspector Getu, who says he comes from a family with close ties to athletics, was interviewed by Dereje Tegenaw about the plan he has brought to lead this federation - an institution that is said to suffer from organisational gaps, problems in athlete selection and recruitment, in the selection and grading of trainees, and in the limits of managers' responsibilities, that is, the certification process and related challenges.

Reporter: The Ethiopian Athletics Federation has produced great athletes who have won international recognition and fame, yet it is said to have gaps in its organisation and its working practices. With what kind of plan have you come forward for election to lead this institution?

Inspector Getu: Given the way Ethiopian athletics has been handed down from generation to generation, and as an Ethiopian who loves the sport, it astonishes and pains me that the institution is now and then a source of dispute and quarrel. Because athletics, like it or not, is not only a signature expression of our diplomacy but also a symbol of our victories. It has also become a major investment option. If the sport stands at that level, then why have we failed to give it, and organise for it, a stature that befits it? That regret still goes round and round inside me. I have come forward as a candidate for the contest, and if I am given the opportunity I am ready to modernise the institution. By profession I am an electrical engineer; the institution I lead is the Ethiopian Electric Utility, where my responsibility is Deputy Chief Executive Officer. As deputy board chairman of the athletics, football and tennis clubs administered under the institution I lead, I have worked - and continue to work - with my colleagues to reform all three clubs so that they have better organisation than other sports clubs in the country. I have a special love and respect for athletics; four members of my family are athletes. As for me, although I did not pursue it far because of my interest in education, I was a runner from my school days. For the past two decades or so I have been carrying out various activities supporting and assisting athletics, starting from training facilities. It is this experience of mine that has become the basis for me to lead this great institution. Certainly, if I get the opportunity, I will work to give the institution, starting from its organisation, the right stature that befits the times, and I will achieve it.

Reporter: It is said that the federation is not being led properly. How do you describe this?

Inspector Getu: When I say I am close to the sport, I mean I know and hear what the gaps and problems observed inside it, as a national institution, look like. I know how sport is led and what sports leadership is, because it is a sector I have been in for the past six years. Beyond that, through the discussions we hold with the federation's leaders and professionals on various work occasions, I know at close hand what the disagreements that arise there are, including their causes. Since I had the opportunity to attend the last two or three Olympics as well as the World Athletics Championships at my own expense, I have come to know and understand, as a person in administration, how and why the gaps arose and what their solutions are. I do not believe that this is an institution you can lead merely because you ran for the house or because you know the science of running. So if you ask me what the institution lacks, it is leadership quality. I do not say this idly: from Rio to the Paris Olympics there were athletes with the capacity to bring three or more gold medals. But as everyone knows, simply because it was not possible to coordinate them owing to the existing problem, the results disappeared. In this respect, with the experience and exposure I have, I am both competent and ready to correct and lead the institution. I am coming to the institution to be part of the solution by holding open and participatory discussions with stakeholders and by preparing systems and directives that address the grievances and complaints of athletes who weep when the Olympics and the World Athletics Championships come round. Personally, if a criterion that everyone agrees on and believes in could be jointly drawn up six months or more before the selection, the arguments and squabbles we now hear could not exist. When the criterion is issued, if the professionals close to this, the club leaders and other relevant stakeholders get the chance to participate in it, to deliberate on it and to decide on it, then everything has found a solution. A leader is not expected to be a coach or a technical expert; what is expected of him is to pass the opportunity down to the relevant departments. I do not believe it will be difficult for me to do this - not only because I am a person who leads a large institution, but also because I have the love for it. It is also easy. Because my personality, starting from my educational background, allows me to go down and work at regional, district and club level to develop athletes, I am ready to lead the federation properly and appropriately.

Reporter: Athletics has now become a sector that captures many people's interests and emotions, and beyond that one in which political and religious tendencies are reflected. How ready are you to lead it in harmony with the laws by which the sport is governed?

Inspector Getu: The problems raised are seen to be widely reflected in the sport. The laws stipulate that sport is free from ethnicity, gender, culture, neighbourhood, language, race and similar things. Sport goes beyond the village; it does not fit the outlook of a single village - rather, it is a sector with great meaning beyond that. Therefore, to lead it while keeping this order, it is proper to talk and discuss with the relevant bodies and to put a system in place. As for the matter of foreign currency and the managers, I often hear the issue raised. The solution requires identifying and formulating the division of responsibilities, setting that down and continuing on that basis. Regarding the benefit the country should get from this sport, I am certain that if the system and the divisions of responsibility are put in place, I do not think there will be an athlete's manager who does not respect that. Because it is known that these same managers work in the same sector in Kenya and other such countries while respecting systems and directives. I see no reason why it should be different in Ethiopia. Rather, in my time managers will have to build camps and academies. If they do not implement that, and if they do not respect the directives and regulations I described earlier, it will be hard for them. Because in neighbouring Kenya we are seeing managers engaged in the same line of work building many camps, raising and developing young people, and producing athletes who set various records in the world. In Kenya itself I had the opportunity to see a camp called 'Iten'. So if the system is put in place and there is proper follow-up, I do not think there will be a manager who breaks away from it. It is true that enforcing the system is not only a matter everyone should follow with a sense of ownership; it is also necessary to accept and acknowledge that it is an obligation of goodwill, so that the country obtains the foreign currency it deserves from this sport and so that sports infrastructure expands. That is why I was compelled to believe earlier that the institution has a leadership gap. What is surprising is that although Ethiopia has produced great and highly esteemed athletes in the athletics world, we have never seen it have even a single representative in international sports institutions. This is a problem that comes from nowhere else but a leadership gap - that is my personal feeling. Through the opportunity I have had to move around in various countries, I have had the chance to speak with many people, including World Athletics leaders. My aim is not to remain here, but to enable Ethiopia to obtain the place it deserves at World Athletics level, including in diplomacy.

Reporter: There are people who link the decline of athletics to the dissolution of the national team. How would you describe your view on this issue?

Inspector Getu: If there is a question I always want to be asked, it is this one. Among the fundamental things that enable Ethiopia to appear beautiful and bright on various international sports stages, the matter of the national team is the foremost. When one thinks of the country, the matter of the national team should be thought of first. A scattered team has no capacity. On this issue, without going far, it is enough to look at the national team that existed in the era of Dr Woldemeskel Kostre. It is a recent memory of ours how the unity of spirit (team spirit) of our athletes alone made them winners. We remember how astonishing was the respect they gave to their flag in perfect brotherhood and sisterhood - beyond the gold medals they won and recorded at the Olympics and the World Athletics Championships. That period left an unforgettable mark on the generation. At present, even when a medal is recorded, we do not see that kind of spirit of the past. Why? Because nothing has been done. If I am asked for the reason, it is, without any hesitation, the dissolution or scattering of the national team. I also see it as a big gap. Because the gap is wide, if I get the opportunity - since the matter concerns many stakeholders - I believe we will achieve it by discussing and deliberating together. Restoring the spirit of cooperation and unity that has been lost in athletics will be my main area of work.

Reporter: It is believed that there is a shortcoming associated with the coaches' grading (certification) process. What kind of plan do you have on this?

Inspector Getu: The matter indeed needs deliberation, but in my view I believe it is necessary to look at the matter in three parts. Because placing the professional at the level (grade) that befits him is decisive. And after the coach's level (certification) has been determined, since it must be implemented by correctly distinguishing between the youth team, the junior team or the senior team, the work is one of my main plans. I also believe that we must talk openly here, because among the matters that have been a cause of differences within the institution is not only the certification issue but also the question of who did what in connection with foreign travel; so the procedure has to be clearly formulated and set down. That is because I believe that a person who has worked must get the value of his toil and effort.

Reporter: It is known that the issue of training facilities is a major challenge for the federation. What is your plan in this regard?

Inspector Getu: It cannot be denied that the former athletes of ours whom we now see engaged in various investment sectors in Ethiopia attained great recognition after passing through much suffering and difficult conditions. At present, to think that we will be successful with the old kind of approach and training methods seems to me to be naivety. Today, for results, alongside training and running, it is a time when much research, food and nutrition styles, training venues, coaching and related matters are included. We are at a point where better training facilities must of necessity be built and constructed. If this is not done, the time when our much-talked-about and much-longed-for athletics pays a price will not be far off. It is necessary to make it possible for small training facilities to be built which the community itself owns and administers in its own area. Beyond this, it is necessary in Ethiopia to do persuasion work with the likes of Ethiopian Airlines and Ethio Telecom, as well as the institution I lead, so that they support the sport and become owners of it. With regard to facilities such as tracks, it is necessary to work together with equipment-manufacturing companies such as Adidas and Nike and with managers. In the institution where I am, I am starting work to lay a track in the Gofa Electric Power area. If I get the opportunity and come to the institution, I have a plan to work together with the relevant stakeholders to alleviate the problem we have at this level. In addition, I am ready to carry out work that includes increasing tracks in the low-lying parts of our country and enabling athletes to live at high altitude. Above all, since it is proper to bring veteran athletes closer to the institution so that they share their advice, knowledge and experience, I will work to make this happen.

a830.t:
O Governo norte-americano, liderado por Donald Trump, anunciou, na noite de ontem, o fim das operações da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID), criada em 1961 e considerada durante décadas a maior distribuidora de ajuda humanitária do mundo.
A USAID estava em processo de desmantelamento desde Fevereiro, quando começaram os cortes nas despesas públicas promovidos pelo magnata Elon Musk, mas, a partir de hoje, o Departamento de Estado assume a gestão total de toda a assistência internacional dos EUA.
O secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, citado por RTP, frisou em comunicado que a USAID não cumpriu os seus objetivos desde o fim da Guerra Fria, além de ter criado uma rede de organizações não-governamentais (ONG) que viveram “à custa dos contribuintes americanos”.
“Esta era de ineficiência chegou oficialmente ao fim. Sob a administração Trump, finalmente teremos uma ajuda externa que prioriza os nossos interesses nacionais”, vincou.
Para Rubio, os cidadãos norte-americanos “não devem pagar impostos para financiar governos falidos em países distantes” e prometeu que, a partir de agora, “a ajuda será direcionada e limitada no tempo”.
Durante o processo de encerramento, foi anunciado que, dos cerca de 10 mil funcionários e contratados da agência em Washington e dos seus escritórios em todo o mundo, apenas 294 permaneceriam para manter as operações mínimas.
O fim da USAID foi muito criticado por especialistas em ajuda humanitária e organizações internacionais, que alertam que o seu desaparecimento deixa uma enorme lacuna nos programas de saúde, educação e resposta a crises humanitárias.
Os ex-presidentes norte-americanos Barack Obama e George W. Bush endereçaram, na segunda-feira, raras críticas ao Governo Trump, enquanto o cantor Bono emocionou-se ao recitar um poema, num evento de despedida da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID).
Um estudo coordenado pelo Instituto de Saúde Global de Barcelona (ISGlobal) e publicado na revista The Lancet alertou que os cortes na ajuda norte-americana podem levar a mais de 14 milhões de mortes `evitáveis` até 2030.
De acordo com o estudo, a USAID teve um impacto fundamental na redução da mortalidade por VIH/SIDA, malária e doenças tropicais negligenciadas em todo o mundo.
A USAID foi criada em 1961 pelo presidente John F. Kennedy para canalizar a ajuda externa americana para fins de desenvolvimento e assistência humanitária.
a830.en:
USAID closes its doors after six decades of humanitarian operations worldwide

The US government, led by Donald Trump, announced last night the end of the operations of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), created in 1961 and considered for decades the world's largest distributor of humanitarian aid.

USAID had been in the process of being dismantled since February, when the cuts in public spending promoted by the magnate Elon Musk began, but from today the State Department takes over full management of all US international assistance.

The Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, quoted by RTP, stressed in a statement that USAID had not fulfilled its objectives since the end of the Cold War, and had also created a network of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that lived "at the expense of American taxpayers".

"This era of inefficiency has officially come to an end. Under the Trump administration, we will finally have foreign aid that prioritises our national interests," he stressed.

For Rubio, American citizens "should not pay taxes to finance bankrupt governments in distant countries", and he promised that from now on "aid will be targeted and limited in time".

During the closure process, it was announced that, of the roughly 10,000 employees and contractors of the agency in Washington and its offices around the world, only 294 would remain to maintain minimum operations.

The end of USAID was heavily criticised by humanitarian aid experts and international organisations, who warn that its disappearance leaves an enormous gap in health, education and humanitarian crisis response programmes.

Former US presidents Barack Obama and George W. Bush on Monday directed rare criticism at the Trump government, while the singer Bono became emotional as he recited a poem at a farewell event for the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

A study coordinated by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) and published in the journal The Lancet warned that the cuts to American aid could lead to more than 14 million 'preventable' deaths by 2030.

According to the study, USAID had a fundamental impact in reducing mortality from HIV/AIDS, malaria and neglected tropical diseases worldwide.

USAID was created in 1961 by President John F. Kennedy to channel American foreign aid for development and humanitarian assistance purposes.

a838.t:
Nous présentons dans ces colonnes, en substance, le communiqué final émis à l’issue des travaux du 8e sommet du Comité de haut niveau de l’Union Africaine sur la Libye qui s’est tenu le 30 janvier dernier au Congo Brazzaville.
Le Comité de haut niveau de l’Union africaine (UA) sur la Libye a tenu sa réunion au niveau des chefs d’État et de Gouvernement, à Brazzaville, en république du Congo, le 30 Janvier 2020, pour étudier l’évolution de la situation en Libye.
Les membres du Comité ont exprimé leur profonde préoccupation au sujet de la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire, humanitaire et économique en Libye, rendant les conditions de vie des populations de plus en plus difficiles. Cette situation en Libye nourrit les réseaux terroristes, criminels et autres trafiquants d’êtres humains qui déstabilisent plusieurs pays de la sous-région.
Le Comité a réaffirmé sa solidarité avec le peuple libyen, son ferme attachement à l’intégrité territoriale du pays, à son unité nationale et à son indépendance. A cet égard, le comité a pris note de l’offre de l’Algérie en vue de rapprocher les différentes vues et a réitéré son engagement à promouvoir le retour aux négociations et ce conformément aux décisions antérieures de l’Union Africaine sur la réconciliation en Libye tout en rappelant la décision prise précédemment par la conférence des chefs d’état d’organiser à Addis Abeba un forum de réconciliation nationale inter-lybienne .
Le Comité apprécie les efforts des pays voisins de la Libye et les sacrifices consentis pour venir en aide aux populations libyennes affectées par la crise et appelle à la poursuite de cet effort en conformité avec les décisions de la conférence des chefs d’état et de gouvernement.
Le Comité s’est engagé en faveur du dialogue politique libyen en rappelant l’urgence d’un dialogue inclusif réunissant toutes les parties libyennes pour promouvoir la cessation du conflit et la recherche d’une solution libyenne à la crise, prenant en considération les intérêts supérieurs du peuple libyen.
Le Comité a condamné fermement la poursuite des combats dans la capitale Tripoli et ses environs et a réitéré l’urgence d’un cessez-le-feu complet et effectif accompagné d’un mécanisme de surveillance dans lequel l’Union africaine sera associée. A cet effet, le Comité a appelé les Etats membres de l’Union africaine à déployer des observateurs militaires, une fois les conditions réunies, pour participer au mécanisme de surveillance du cessez-le-feu et être en lien avec les parties libyennes.
Le Comité a condamné la poursuite des interférences extérieures en Libye au lendemain des engagements pris à Berlin et a renouvelé son appel à tous les acteurs extérieurs pour qu’ils cessent immédiatement toute ingérence dans les affaires intérieures de la Libye notamment la livraison d’armes et le recrutement de mercenaires, qui exacerbent la crise avec des conséquences sur la vie des personnes et qui menacent les intérêts fondamentaux du peuple libyen et ses aspirations légitimes à la liberté, à la paix, à la démocratie et au développement.
Le Comité a insisté sur le strict respect de l’embargo décrété par le Conseil de sécurité sur les armes en Libye. Il a appelé ce dernier à appliquer les sanctions prévues en cas de violation.
Le Comité a condamné énergiquement les activités terroristes, l’emploi des combattants étrangers et le recours aux mercenaires, ainsi que toute facilitation de transit, de transport ou de recrutement illégaux en violation la Convention de l’OUA sur l’Elimination du Mercenariat en Afrique du 03 juillet 1977.
Le Comité a exprimé sa préoccupation compte tenu du niveau sans précèdent de la circulation d’armes sophistiquées en Libye, qui aggrave le conflit et menace la paix et la sécurité du pays des Etats voisins et du Sahel. Par ailleurs, le Comité a appelé la Commission de l’Union africaine à veiller à la mise en œuvre des mécanismes de lutte contre la criminalité et le terrorisme transfrontaliers par les Etats membres.
Vivement préoccupé par la dégradation de la situation humanitaire en Libye, le Comité a appelé à la protection internationale des migrants africains détenus et retenus en Libye et utilisés comme combattants et boucliers humains et faciliter leurs rapatriement dans leurs pays d’origine.
Le Comité a appelé à la mobilisation de l’aide humanitaire en faveur des populations vulnérables, des réfugiés et des déplacés internes. Le Comité a lancé également un appel aux parties belligérantes de veiller au strict respect du Droit International Humanitaire, notamment par la sécurisation des hôpitaux, des écoles ainsi que la facilitation de l’acheminement de l’aide.
Le Comité de Haut Niveau a souligné le principe de la souveraineté permanente des peuples sur leurs ressources naturelles et réaffirme que celles-ci en sont la propriété du peuple libyen. Ainsi, le Comité a appelé à la réouverture, des terminaux pétroliers en vue de permettre au peuple libyen de profiter pleinement de ses ressources.
Le Comité a rappelé que les installations portuaires et aéroportuaires civiles doivent être mises au service des citoyens libyens et placées en dehors de toute activité militaire mettant en péril la vie des civils ou les empêchant de bénéficier des services de ces installations.
Le Comité a décidé de préparer et de tenir la Conférence inter-libyenne de Réconciliation conformément aux décisions pertinentes de l’Union Africaine, en concertation avec les pays voisins et les Nations Unies.
Dans cet ordre d’idées, le Comité a décidé de créer une Commission Préparatoire Inclusive de ladite conférence. Celle-ci doit être ouverte à toutes les parties prenantes libyennes y compris les chefs des tribus, les femmes et les jeunes et autres forces politiques et sociales pour promouvoir une solution durable au conflit.
En outre, le Comité a adopté une Feuille de Route fixant les principales étapes de ce processus. Cette feuille de route décide de la création de la Commission préparatoire du forum, du calendrier de ses réunions, et statue sur les ressources humaines et financières requises pour le succès de sa mission.
a838.en:
What does the final communiqué say?

We present in these columns, in substance, the final communiqué issued at the end of the work of the 8th summit of the African Union High-Level Committee on Libya, which was held on 30 January at Congo Brazzaville.

The African Union (AU) High-Level Committee on Libya held its meeting at the level of Heads of State and Government, in Brazzaville, in the Republic of Congo, on 30 January 2020, to examine developments in the situation in Libya.

The members of the Committee expressed their deep concern about the deterioration of the security, humanitarian and economic situation in Libya, making living conditions for the population increasingly difficult. This situation in Libya feeds the terrorist and criminal networks and other human traffickers who are destabilising several countries of the sub-region.

The Committee reaffirmed its solidarity with the Libyan people, its firm attachment to the territorial integrity of the country, to its national unity and to its independence. In this regard, the Committee took note of Algeria's offer to bring the different views closer together and reiterated its commitment to promoting a return to negotiations, in accordance with previous African Union decisions on reconciliation in Libya, while recalling the decision taken previously by the conference of heads of state to organise in Addis Ababa an inter-Libyan national reconciliation forum.

The Committee appreciates the efforts of Libya's neighbouring countries and the sacrifices made to come to the aid of the Libyan populations affected by the crisis and calls for the continuation of this effort in conformity with the decisions of the conference of heads of state and government.

The Committee committed itself in favour of the Libyan political dialogue, recalling the urgency of an inclusive dialogue bringing together all the Libyan parties to promote the cessation of the conflict and the search for a Libyan solution to the crisis, taking into consideration the higher interests of the Libyan people.

The Committee firmly condemned the continuation of the fighting in the capital Tripoli and its surroundings and reiterated the urgency of a complete and effective ceasefire accompanied by a monitoring mechanism in which the African Union will be associated. To this end, the Committee called on the member states of the African Union to deploy military observers, once conditions are met, to participate in the ceasefire monitoring mechanism and to be in contact with the Libyan parties.

The Committee condemned the continuation of external interference in Libya in the aftermath of the commitments made in Berlin and renewed its call to all external actors to cease immediately all interference in the internal affairs of Libya, notably the delivery of weapons and the recruitment of mercenaries, which exacerbate the crisis with consequences for people's lives and which threaten the fundamental interests of the Libyan people and its legitimate aspirations to freedom, peace, democracy and development.

The Committee insisted on strict respect for the embargo decreed by the Security Council on weapons in Libya. It called on the latter to apply the sanctions provided for in case of violation.

The Committee energetically condemned terrorist activities, the use of foreign fighters and recourse to mercenaries, as well as any facilitation of illegal transit, transport or recruitment in violation of the OAU Convention on the Elimination of Mercenarism in Africa of 3 July 1977.

The Committee expressed its concern given the unprecedented level of circulation of sophisticated weapons in Libya, which aggravates the conflict and threatens the peace and security of the country, of neighbouring States and of the Sahel. Moreover, the Committee called on the African Union Commission to ensure the implementation of mechanisms to combat cross-border crime and terrorism by the member states.

Deeply concerned by the degradation of the humanitarian situation in Libya, the Committee called for the international protection of African migrants detained and held in Libya and used as fighters and human shields, and to facilitate their repatriation to their countries of origin.

The Committee called for the mobilisation of humanitarian aid in favour of vulnerable populations, refugees and internally displaced persons. The Committee also launched an appeal to the belligerent parties to ensure strict respect for International Humanitarian Law, notably through the securing of hospitals and schools as well as the facilitation of the delivery of aid.

The High-Level Committee underlined the principle of the permanent sovereignty of peoples over their natural resources and reaffirms that these are the property of the Libyan people. Thus, the Committee called for the reopening of the oil terminals with a view to allowing the Libyan people to profit fully from its resources.

The Committee recalled that civilian port and airport installations must be placed at the service of Libyan citizens and placed outside any military activity endangering the lives of civilians or preventing them from benefiting from the services of these installations.

The Committee decided to prepare and hold the inter-Libyan Reconciliation Conference in conformity with the relevant decisions of the African Union, in consultation with the neighbouring countries and the United Nations.

In this line of thinking, the Committee decided to create an Inclusive Preparatory Commission for the said conference. This must be open to all Libyan stakeholders including tribal chiefs, women and young people and other political and social forces in order to promote a lasting solution to the conflict.

In addition, the Committee adopted a Roadmap setting out the main stages of this process. This roadmap decides on the creation of the preparatory commission of the forum, the calendar of its meetings, and rules on the human and financial resources required for the success of its mission.

a872.t:
Grâce au Millennium Challenge Account Bénin II, la commune d’Abomey-Calavi  bénéficie d’un stade aux normes de la Fédération internationale de Football Associations dans l’arrondissement d’Akassato. Achevé le 10 juin dernier, ce terrain a été mis en exploitation, jeudi 22 juin dernier, en marge de l'inauguration du Centre national de contrôle de la distribution d’électricité à Akassato. C’était en présence d’Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, ministre d’Etat en charge du Développement et de la Coordination de l’action gouvernementale et président du conseil d’administration du Mca-Bénin II, de Brian Shukan, ambassadeur des États-Unis près le Bénin et d’Alice Albright, présidente directrice générale du Millennium challenge corporation (Mcc). Dotée d’une pelouse synthétique (100 x 65 Cm), cette infrastructure est réalisée en compensation de l'occupation de la précédente aire de jeux de cet arrondissement par le Centre national de Contrôle de la distribution d’électricité d’Akassato. A travers ce joyau, Mca-Bénin II assure la continuité des activités sportives aux jeunes. 
A cette occasion, Brian Shukan, ambassadeur des États-Unis près le Bénin, s’est réjoui de la mise en exploitation de l’ouvrage, fruit de la coopération entre le Bénin et les Etats-Unis. « Le Mca-Bénin II est le meilleur symbole de la coopération entre le Bénin et les États-Unis, qui dure depuis 60 ans », a-t-il déclaré.  
Pour sa part, Gabriel Dégbègni, coordonnateur national du Mca Bénin II, se dit fier de faire le bilan des nouvelles infrastructures dont le pays bénéficie. « C'est une fierté pour le personnel du Mca-Bénin II qui a surmonté bon nombre de défis pour réaliser les objectifs », a-t-il fait remarquer. Abdoulaye Bio Tchané se réjouit de la mise en œuvre du Mca-Bénin II qui impacte 12 millions de Béninois et qui ouvre des perspectives pour l'essor économique du Bénin grâce à la disponibilité de l'électricité. « Le Compact est le meilleur outil de financement du développement », a-t-il confié.
a872.en:
Thanks to the Millennium Challenge Account Benin II, the commune of Abomey-Calavi is benefiting from a stadium built to the standards of the International Federation of Association Football in the Akassato district. Completed on 10 June, this pitch was brought into use on Thursday 22 June, on the sidelines of the inauguration of the National Electricity Distribution Control Centre at Akassato. It took place in the presence of Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and Chairman of the Board of Directors of MCA-Benin II, of Brian Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin, and of Alice Albright, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC). Fitted with a synthetic lawn (100 x 65 m), this infrastructure was built as compensation for the occupation of the district’s previous playing field by the National Electricity Distribution Control Centre of Akassato. Through this gem, MCA-Benin II ensures the continuity of sporting activities for young people.

On this occasion, Brian Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin, welcomed the entry into service of the facility, the fruit of cooperation between Benin and the United States. “MCA-Benin II is the best symbol of the cooperation between Benin and the United States, which has lasted for 60 years,” he declared.

For his part, Gabriel Dégbègni, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin II, says he is proud to take stock of the new infrastructure the country is benefiting from. “It is a source of pride for the staff of MCA-Benin II, who overcame a good number of challenges to achieve the objectives,” he remarked. Abdoulaye Bio Tchané welcomed the implementation of MCA-Benin II, which impacts 12 million Beninese and which opens prospects for Benin’s economic development thanks to the availability of electricity. “The Compact is the best development financing tool,” he confided.

a1053.t:
Bulawayo, (New Ziana) –The Zimbabwe government recognises the vital role that Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play in driving economic growth, job creation, and sustainable development in the country, a cabinet Minister has said.
Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development Monica Mutsvangwa said this on Friday while openeing a a four-day MSME training manual validation workshop in Bulawayo. The four-day workshop also included the training of Trainers for the Ministry’s Business and Cooperative Development officers drawn from the Head Office and the country’s 10 provinces.
The training, supported by the Division for Sustainable Development Goals under the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNDESA), was aimed at equipping MSMEs with business resilience, management, and digital skills.
The development of the MSME Training Manual marks a significant milestone following the MSME Results Monitoring Framework and Southern Region Business Management training launched in Zimbabwe in June 2022. “MSMEs contribute significantly to value addition, exports growth, and providing essential ancillary services across sectors.
“Therefore, government recognises the substantial role played by MSMEs in driving economic growth and sustainable development in Zimbabwe through creating jobs, providing key ancillary services in almost all sectors of the economy, driving value addition and export growth,” the minister said.
Mutsvangwa highlighted that the MSME sector employs 4.8 million people on a full-time basis and contributes more than 60% to the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), according to the 2021 MSMEs Survey. She however acknowledged several challenges that the sector faces, including limited access to finance, markets, appropriate workspaces, and insufficient business management skills. “Furthermore, it must be noted that the business environment is marked by uncertainty, economic shocks, and rapid changes.
“There is therefore a need for robust and coordinated supportive mechanisms by all stakeholders to build the capacity of SMEs to survive in this environment,” she said. Mutsvangwa said her ministry remains committed to providing MSMEs with resources, training, and opportunities to unlock their potential. “Guided by the MSMEs Policy Framework (2020–2024), the Ministry is implementing a number of programs meant to address these challenges.
“These initiatives include funding through the Women Development Fund (WDF), Community Development Fund (CDF), Zimbabwe Women Microfinance Bank (ZWMB), and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Corporation (SMEDCO), construction of MSMEs factory shells to ensure MSMEs have decent workspaces, business management skills training, assisting MSMEs to exhibit their products and services at various exhibitions and expos locally and internationally, among others,” she explained.
Mutsvangwa commended UNDESA for supporting the development of the manual saying it will positively enhance the capacity of MSMEs to manage and grow their businesses in a highly competitive business environment. She also emphasized the importance of sustainable risk management practices for MSMEs, citing the recent fire at the Mbare Traders’ Market, where traders lost millions worth of goods.
New Ziana

a1140.t:
The female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) calls for the protection of female Journalists here.
Bomi County, Liberia, November 27, 2024 –As the world commemorates 16 Days of Activism to end all forms of violence against women and girls, Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) is calling for a safe working environment for women journalists across Liberia.
Aligned with this year’s global theme: “Towards Beijing +30: UNiTE to End Violence Against Women and Girls,” and national theme “From Talk to Action! Let’s Join Hands to End Violence Against Women and Girls,” FeJAL says it will utilize the media through advocacy, talkshows and social media campaigns to raise public awareness on the need to protect rights of women journalists in Liberia.
In a press statement, FeJAL says these discussions will focus on critical topics such as challenges faced by women journalists in the newsroom, promoting safe workspaces, protecting their rights, and supporting women’s leadership in the media.
The advocacy talkshow kicked off with a panel discussion on the Liberia Broadcasting System (ELBC) on Monday November 25, 2024 and will continue in the counties, leveraging the USAID Media Activity Partner stations which will feature its county coordinators to discuss similarly.
FeJAL aims to mobilize media stakeholders, change dynamics on promoting a workspace free of intimidation, harassment and exploitation of women in the media during these 16days of activism.
FeJAL is committed to contributing to the global and national efforts to end violence against women and girls, promote safe working environments for women journalists, and empower women and girls with necessary resources and support networks.
Through collective action and collaboration, FeJAL believes that concrete steps can be taken to create lasting change for the betterment of women journalists in Liberia.
The Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) is a leading media development organization with a national presence across 15 counties in Liberia. It is established to advance advocacy for rights of women journalists in Liberia. Press Release

a1146.t:
Former Proteas fast bowler Dale Steyn is among 17 former male and female international cricketers named an Honorary Life Member of the MCC.
Steyn is joined by another South African-born player, Kevin Petersen, who represented England from 2005 to 2014.
Steyn played for South Africa from 2004 to 2020 before retiring.
During his career, he took 439 Test wickets at an average of 22.95 and a strike rate of 42.3.
Steyn also claimed 196 wickets in one-day internationals and a further 64 in T20 internationals for 699 wickets overall for South Africa.
He is the current bowling coach of IPL franchise Sunrisers Hyderabad.
Guy Lavender, Chief Executive & Secretary of MCC, said: "We are thrilled to be able to announce our newest cohort of Honorary Life Members of MCC as we prepare for the new international summer.
"The names that have been announced today are some of the greatest international players of modern times, and we are privileged to now count them as valued Members of our Club.
"We are also pleased to be able to announce two individuals who have been awarded this honour for their monumental contributions off the pitch."
